reason: The sole cited evidence (E1) discusses wear-induced nanostructured oxide layer formation in HEAs under frictional heat, which is unrelated to pulsed laser remelting, nanocrystalline layer formation via rapid solidification, or the preservation of bulk caloric properties. No evidence supports any of the key premises.
premises: Pulsed laser remelting can form a nanocrystalline surface layer in this specific alloy.
A nanocrystalline surface layer reduces defect density and improves crack resistance/fatigue life.
The treatment can be confined to a shallow (50-100 μm) surface layer.
The bulk microstructure and its caloric phase transitions remain intact after surface laser treatment.
The caloric performance (entropy change, reversibility) will be preserved.
